answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify useful work. If a newcomer tries to flood the network with sybils, every identity needs its own stake and must risk losing it for fraud; splitting one stake across a pearl, vine, and thread of fake accounts does not multiply voting weight. The attacker therefore pays upfront capital and faces slashing, while honest agents can build reputation over time.
